references.text: The Lord promises to lead Israel into the land of the Canaanites, a land flowing with milk and honey.
God confirms his promise to bring the people out of Egypt and into the land of the Canaanites.
The Lord promises to give the land to Israel, just as he swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God's covenant with Abraham in which he promises to give the land to his descendants.
God promises Abraham the whole land of Canaan as an eternal possession.
God confirms the oath he swore to Abraham to give the land to his offspring.
God repeats the promise to Jacob to give him and his descendants the land.
Joseph reminds them of God's oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to bring them into the promised land.
Reference to the oath God swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to give them the land.
When the Lord brings you into the land he swore to give your fathers.
God brought Israel out of Egypt to give them the land he had promised their fathers.
When the Lord brings you into the land and drives out the Canaanites before you.
Confirmation of the arrival in the land that the Lord swore to give to the fathers.
Deuteronomy 26:1 specifies the entry and takeover as the historical fulfillment of the oath-promise mentioned in Exodus.
Both verses emphasize that the giving of the land is founded on an oath sworn to the fathers, even though the timing (entry versus expansion) varies.
The verses are parallel accounts of the same event; 13:5 provides details about the peoples and the nature of the land that are missing in 13:11.
Direct narrative connection; 12:25 sets up the instruction to be carried out at the entry described in 13:11.
